The Nobel Prize in Physics for the year 2021 was jointly awarded to Syukuro Manabe, Klaus Hasselmann, and Giorgio Parisi "for groundbreaking contributions to our understanding of complex systems". Syukuro Manabe, a Japanese meteorologist, was recognized for his work on the mathematical modeling of the Earth's atmosphere, which helped to establish the field of climate physics. Klaus Hasselmann, a German physicist, was recognized for his work on understanding and predicting climate variability, which has contributed to our ability to make more accurate climate forecasts. Giorgio Parisi, an Italian theoretical physicist, was recognized for his work on disordered systems, which has led to a better understanding of complex phenomena such as spin glasses and neural networks.

The Nobel Prize in Physics for 2022 was awarded to Sir Roger Penrose and Dr. Andrea Ghez "for their discoveries about the evolution of the universe and black holes." Sir Roger Penrose, an emeritus professor at the University of Oxford, is known for his work on black holes and the theory of general relativity. Dr. Andrea Ghez, a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles, was recognized for her research on the centers of galaxies, including the discovery of a supermassive black hole at the Milky Way's core. The Nobel Prizes are awarded annually, and the winners are selected by the Nobel Committee for Physics, which is responsible for awarding the Nobel Prize in Physics.
